input.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: full-room concept for the GamifySurgery 3 x 3 hospital Gift Shop; this entire room is the design source, not a collection of isolated assets.
Input images: image 1 is the 3 x 3 Wound/Ostomy Clinic room to transform, retaining its camera, room footprint, straight rear wall and cutaway front. Image 2 is the approved Pediatric Waiting Room, only a finish, outline, palette and game-art reference.
Replace the medical furniture and room contents with one cohesive, densely stocked little hospital gift shop. Preserve the exact front-elevated orthographic game view: straight horizontal back wall, vertical side boundaries, square 3 x 3 tiled floor, no rotated isometric room, no vanishing point. Match the game's crisp raster pixel-art edges, fine dark green/brown outlines, small shaded color clusters and warm subdued colors, not a glossy 3D illustration.
Room-first composition: substantial sage-and-honeywood shelving runs line the entire back wall edge to edge in three adjoining bays. They are packed with overlapping teddy bears and plush toys, blank patterned greeting cards, plain snack packages, magazines with abstract covers, mugs and candles. Fixtures have full-width plinths on the floor, not thin legs or tiny footprints. Tall flowers in crowded buckets and a glass flower cooler join the left-wall card racks, continuing all the way to the front-left corner. Low magazine/snack shelves and overflowing plush bins line the right wall as one continuous run, down to a crowded balloon-and-flower bucket at the front-right entrance corner. Balloons overlap in the back-left corner and above the entrance display. All fixture runs sit FLUSH against the walls and abut each other; goods overlap neighboring shelving silhouettes. No isolated objects floating in empty space.
A compact joined honeywood main-display and self-service checkout island occupies roughly one floor tile in the middle, slightly left of center. Its rear half is a dense flower-and-teddy display; its front half is the checkout counter with a small shopper-facing screen and card terminal. Pack impulse snacks, blank cards and little gift items around the terminal. The island has a broad filled base, no airy pedestal. A small sage checkout mat sits directly in front.
Leave one connected shopping aisle forming a loop around this island, with the broadest lane on the right for two queued standing shoppers; front-center entry joins that aisle, goes past displays to the south-facing checkout and back out. The floor should read mostly as fixtures extending upward from occupied floor area, plus this deliberately shaped aisle, not a broad empty room. Floor tile edges merely establish the 3 x 3 footprint. Front wall is low cutaway, central entrance open. No shoppers or staff in this concept, no readable text, no letters, no numerals, no brands, no labels, no watermark. Keep the entire room visible, without cropping the fixtures or room border.
